newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack details London rail link plans.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack details London rail link plans.

text.p: UK rail operator Railtrack Plc on Wednesday detailed its service plan for London's north-south Thameslink rail project.
The company, privatised by the UK government last year, said the Thameslink 2000 project would cost 560 million stg.
"Subject to the receipt of necessary authorisations...work on this major project is currently planned to start during 1999, with a targeted completion date of 2003," it said in a statement.
Last year Railtrack said the project, aimed at increasing the line's capacity, could have been finished by 2002 if construction began in 1998.
In September Britain's Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) invited tenders for the Thameslink passenger train operating company, which runs trains on the line.
Thameslink serves regional centres north and south of London via the only rail lines through the city centre. Its passenger revenue was 76 million stg in the year to the end of March 1996.
Railtrack said the plans announced on Wednesday included significant routes in Kent, to the south-east of the capital.
This included Dartford, Bromley and Ashford via the town of Tonbridge as additional destinations and the dropping of Bognor Regis and East Grinstead from the original proposals.
The plans also include track modifications to the east of London Bridge "which allow for the additional destinations in Kent and a significantly more reliable day to day operation".
There would also be extra platform capacity for Blackfriars station, it added.
